followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: how well the task matches each model's documented strengths, and (secondarily) the self-reported task preferences.

The query asks for a thorough, complete enumeration of robot components — a closed-ended task with a clear completion criterion ("comprehensive," "don't leave half of it out"). That profile aligns with Willet's self-reported top-rated task family: well-specified retrieval, extraction, and reformatting requests. So the preference fit favored Willet.

On capability, the two models are effectively tied on the relevant dimension: Extraction & Retrieval is 81.6 (Lapwing) vs 79.2 (Willet), and Summarization is essentially equal — differences hovering around the 2.0-point variance threshold, so I don't treat them as decisive.

Given near-equal capability, I broke the tie on preference fit, routing to the model whose documented preferences match the task type. That said, it's worth flagging the dissociation noted in the docs: Willet's preference for these tasks is decoupled from measured quality, so this choice optimizes for preference alignment rather than any expected quality gain — the two models would likely perform comparably here.
